sections.content: If you've been scanning the Mountain West for your next investment opportunity, Ogden, Utah deserves a serious look. Sitting about 35 miles north of Salt Lake City along the Wasatch Front, Ogden has transformed from a post-industrial railroad town into a thriving outdoor recreation hub — and real estate investors are starting to pay attention. Home prices are still relatively affordable compared to Salt Lake City and Provo, inventory remains tight, and population growth is fueling consistent demand for both rentals and move-in-ready homes. Whether you're a seasoned wholesaler or just getting started, this guide covers everything you need to know about finding real estate deals in Ogden UT. If you're brand new to the investing world, check out our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving in.
Ogden UT Real Estate Market Overview

Ogden is the county seat of Weber County and home to roughly 90,000 residents, with the greater metro area pushing closer to 270,000. The city has benefited enormously from Utah's broader economic boom. Major employers include Hill Air Force Base — one of the largest employers in the state with over 22,000 military and civilian workers — along with a growing tech and outdoor recreation industry anchored by brands like Descente, Rossignol, and Scott Sports. Weber State University adds another layer of rental demand, keeping vacancy rates low in many neighborhoods. For a deeper look at local data and active deals, visit the [Ogden UT market page](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/ogden-ut) on AIWholesail.
Average Home Prices in Ogden UT

As of late 2024, the median home price in Ogden sits around $320,000 to $340,000 — well below Salt Lake City's median of roughly $480,000. That price gap is a major draw for investors. Distressed properties and fixer-uppers can still be found in the $180,000 to $250,000 range, while fully renovated homes in desirable neighborhoods are selling between $380,000 and $450,000. This spread creates real room for wholesalers and flippers to generate meaningful margins. Rental rates for single-family homes average $1,400 to $1,900 per month depending on size and location, while multi-family units near Weber State consistently rent for $900 to $1,300 per unit.

Before making an offer on any property in Ogden, run the numbers using our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to estimate after-repair value based on local comparable sales. A solid ARV estimate is the foundation of every profitable deal.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Ogden

Not all of Ogden's zip codes are created equal. Knowing where to focus your energy can be the difference between a great deal and an expensive mistake. Here are the neighborhoods that consistently produce the best opportunities for investors.

items: Downtown Ogden / Central Business District: Urban revitalization is in full swing here. Historic Victorian and Craftsman homes are being renovated, and city incentives make rehab projects more attractive. Great for fix-and-flip investors willing to do their homework.

East Bench: This established neighborhood near the foothills attracts higher-income buyers and strong rental tenants. Homes here hold value well and attract buyers looking for mountain views and proximity to trails.
South Ogden: A stable suburban area with good schools and consistent demand. Solid buy-and-hold territory with lower vacancy rates and reliable rent growth.

Harrisville / North Ogden: These adjacent cities just north of Ogden offer newer housing stock, family-friendly neighborhoods, and growing demand. Less competition from other investors makes off-market deals more accessible.

Washington Terrace: Working-class neighborhood with affordable entry points. Investors targeting the BRRRR strategy (Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat) find good opportunities here due to lower acquisition costs.

Near Weber State University: Student rental demand keeps occupancy high year-round. Multi-family properties within walking distance of campus can generate strong cash flow, especially when managed efficiently.

sections.content: Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Ogden UT
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is alive and active in Ogden, though competition has increased as more investors discover the market. The most successful wholesalers here focus on distressed properties from motivated sellers — think probate situations, pre-foreclosures, tax-delinquent properties, and absentee owners with aging rentals. Assignment fees in Ogden typically range from $8,000 to $20,000 depending on the deal. If you're new to the strategy, our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide walks you through every step. Use our free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to quickly determine your maximum allowable offer (MAO) before submitting a contract.
Fix-and-Flip

Flipping homes in Ogden can be highly profitable when you buy right. The city's older housing stock — many homes were built between 1940 and 1980 — means there's consistent supply of properties needing updates. A typical flip in Ogden might look like this: purchase a distressed property for $210,000, invest $55,000 in renovations, and sell for $320,000, netting a gross profit around $55,000 before holding costs and agent fees. The key is accurate ARV estimation and disciplined rehab budgeting. Local contractors are more accessible than in Salt Lake City, though labor costs have risen with the broader construction boom across Utah.
Buy-and-Hold Rentals

Long-term rental investors are drawn to Ogden's strong employment base, growing population, and relatively low vacancy rates hovering around 4 to 5 percent. Single-family homes in South Ogden and Washington Terrace can pencil out as cash-flow-positive investments, especially when purchased below market. Multi-family properties — duplexes, triplexes, and small apartment buildings — near Weber State offer some of the best cash-on-cash returns in the market, often running 6 to 9 percent in today's rate environment.
Ogden Real Estate Market Trends to Watch

items: Population Growth: Weber County has grown over 12% in the past decade, driven by in-migration from California, Washington, and other high-cost states. This trend shows no signs of slowing.

Infrastructure Investment: The Ogden-Weber Transit District continues expanding bus rapid transit, and the region benefits from proximity to Salt Lake City's TRAX light rail system. Better connectivity increases property values in connected corridors.

Outdoor Recreation Economy: Ogden markets itself as 'Outdoor Recreation Capital of Utah.' Proximity to Snowbasin, Powder Mountain, and Nordic Valley ski resorts drives short-term rental demand and keeps tourism strong.
Hill Air Force Base Expansion: F-35 mission expansions at Hill AFB continue to bring high-income military families to the area, creating consistent demand for quality rental housing in Weber County.
Rising Construction Costs: New construction is lagging behind demand, which supports values for existing homes and reduces competition for renovation-ready properties.
Investor Competition Increasing: Ogden is on more investors' radar than it was three years ago. Moving quickly on quality deals is more important than ever.

sections.content: The best real estate markets aren't the ones everyone is already talking about — they're the ones where the fundamentals are strong and the crowd hasn't fully arrived yet. Ogden is right at that inflection point.
How to Find Off-Market Deals in Ogden UT

On-market deals in Ogden rarely have the margins investors need. The real money is in off-market properties — motivated sellers who haven't listed yet and need a fast, private solution. The most effective strategies include direct mail campaigns targeting absentee owners and tax-delinquent properties, driving for dollars in transitional neighborhoods like Central Ogden and Washington Terrace, connecting with probate attorneys in Weber County, and building relationships with local real estate agents who specialize in distressed or estate sales. For a deeper dive into sourcing strategies, read our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals). Networking with other local investors through the Utah Real Estate Investors Association (UREIA) is also worth your time — deals get passed around at meetups before they ever hit any platform.
Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors

Ogden attracts plenty of interest from out-of-state investors, particularly from California, where capital gains from home sales are being redeployed into more affordable markets. If you're investing remotely, here's how to do it right.

items: Build a local team first: You need a boots-on-the-ground property manager, a reliable contractor, and a transactional real estate attorney familiar with Utah contract law before you close your first deal.
Understand Utah's assignment laws: Utah is relatively investor-friendly, but you should work with a local attorney to ensure your wholesale contracts and assignment clauses are properly structured.

Visit before you commit: A single market visit to walk neighborhoods, meet contractors, and tour properties will save you from costly remote-buying mistakes. Budget one trip before your first acquisition.
Use technology to your advantage: Platforms like AIWholesail can surface distressed and off-market leads in the Ogden market so you're not relying solely on the MLS or wholesaler lists.

Analyze deals conservatively: Remote investors often underestimate rehab costs. Add a 15-20% contingency to any contractor estimate you receive remotely, and always verify ARV using local comps rather than Zillow estimates.

Know your exit strategy before you buy: Whether you plan to wholesale, flip, or hold, have your buyer or tenant pipeline in place before acquiring the property. Carrying costs in Utah's market can erode margins quickly.

Is Ogden UT Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Ogden isn't a get-rich-quick market, but it rewards investors who do their homework. The fundamentals are genuinely strong: population growth, a diverse employment base anchored by a major military installation, a thriving outdoor economy, and home prices that still have room to run compared to the broader Wasatch Front. For wholesalers, there are enough distressed properties to build a consistent pipeline. For flippers, the older housing stock creates renovation opportunities with real spread. For buy-and-hold investors, the rental demand from military families, students, and in-migrants keeps vacancy rates manageable. The window to enter this market at favorable prices may not stay open indefinitely — competition is increasing every year as more investors discover what Ogden has to offer.
